input.memo_markdown:
*All data in this report is synthetic.*

## Last week's moves
First run. There are no prior moves to review.

## What's happening
- **Direct / untracked:** weekly conversions went from 10 (week of 8/3) to 62 (week of 10/26), and revenue from $2.2k to $11.7k. Paid spend was flat. Self-reported "Asked ChatGPT" rose from 0.9% to 19.3%, and "AI assistant recommended you" from 0% to 5%. This looks like AI-assistant referral, not paid.
- **LinkedIn:** CPA is $282.6 over the last 3 weeks vs $195.6 earlier (+45%) on flat spend (-6%). Last-week ROAS is 0.64 vs the 1.5 target.
- **Google Search:** the 9/12-9/18 spend spike (1.79x the median) pushed CPA to about $24. It has fully recovered: CPA is $14.36 and ROAS 13.0 in the latest week.
- **Meta:** CPA is $52.97 over the last 3 weeks vs $58.19 earlier, ROAS 3.1-3.9. Stable.
- **Email:** CPA is $20.94 vs $20.32, stable at about $280/week.

## Moves
- **LinkedIn:** $300 to $240/day (-20%). The CPA rise is sustained, and the channel is below target under last-touch (0.89) and time-decay (1.34). It is not cut further because first-touch (1.9), Markov (1.83) and linear (1.53) are above target.
- **Google, Meta, Email:** no change.

## Where the models disagree
- **LinkedIn:** implied ROAS ranges from 0.89 (last-touch) to 1.9 (first-touch), straddling the 1.5 target.
- **Google:** credit share ranges from 39% (first-touch) to 68% (last-touch). Even at the low end, ROAS is 6.1, far above target.
- **Email:** ROAS ranges from 9.2 (last-touch) to 56 (first-touch). It is under-credited by last-click and is cheap at $40/day, so leave it.

## Test to run
LinkedIn holdout: suppress it for a random 50% of target accounts or regions for 4 weeks. Measure total conversions across all channels in held-out vs exposed groups. Pause it if incremental ROAS is under 1.5.

## Confidence
Medium overall. I would cut LinkedIn harder if the holdout shows lift below break-even. I would revisit the direct reading if self-reported AI answers fall while direct stays high, or if direct falls when a paid channel is cut. Attribution models only see tracked clicks, so none of them can value the AI-driven direct traffic.
